new.title: Admire the Freiberg Cathedral and its Golden Gate
new.desc: Freiberg Cathedral (Dom St. Marien) is a late Gothic hall church whose Romanesque Golden Gate of about 1230 is one of the finest portals in Saxony. It holds two Gottfried Silbermann organs, including the one from 1714, and the Wettin burial chapel.
new.tip: Organ demonstrations and tours run on set days; check the cathedral schedule.
new.q: Freiberger Dom St. Marien, Untermarkt 1, Freiberg

new.title: See 3,500 minerals at terra mineralia in Schloss Freudenstein
new.desc: terra mineralia in Schloss Freudenstein shows the Pohl-Ströher collection of about 3,500 minerals and gemstones from all continents. It belongs to TU Bergakademie Freiberg and sits in the castle rebuilt after the town fire of 1566.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; allow two hours and combine with the Freiberg old town.

new.title: Climb up to Schloss Augustusburg
new.desc: Elector Augustus of Saxony had Augustusburg built on the Schellenberg in 1568-1572 as a hunting lodge, 516 m above sea level and visible from afar. It houses a hunting and a carriage museum, a motorcycle museum and a castle chapel with an altar painting by Lucas Cranach the Younger.
new.tip: A cable car runs up from Erdmannsdorf; check winter hours.

new.title: Stroll the baroque gardens of Schloss Lichtenwalde
new.desc: Schloss Lichtenwalde near Frankenberg was built from 1722 for Christoph Heinrich von Watzdorf and is known for one of the finest baroque garden terraces in Saxony. The park below the castle has water features and a great parterre.
new.tip: Park and castle have seasonal opening hours; check before going.

new.title: Visit Burg Kriebstein above the Zschopau valley
new.desc: Burg Kriebstein stands on a rock above the Zschopau and was built from 1384 under Dietrich von Beerwalde. It is among the best preserved late medieval castles in Saxony with a richly furnished interior.
new.tip: Open daily in season; the trail from the Kriebstein dam is a good approach.

new.title: Tour Schloss Rochlitz on the Mulde
new.desc: Schloss Rochlitz is a Romanesque-Gothic castle above the Zwickauer Mulde with the twin Jupen towers and a former Wettin residence. Its museum covers the Wettins, Margravine Elisabeth and the Reformation.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday in season; the towers give river views.

new.title: Hike the porphyry quarries of the Rochlitzer Berg
new.desc: The Rochlitzer Berg is a hill of red porphyry tuff, quarried for centuries to build Saxon churches and castles. Quarry trails and a lookout tower reveal the stone workings.
new.tip: Free; wear solid shoes and bring water.

new.title: See the late Gothic St. Annenkirche in Annaberg
new.desc: The St. Annenkirche in Annaberg-Buchholz was built 1499-1525 and is the largest late Gothic hall church in the Ore Mountains. Its net vault is carved in stone and the Bergaltar features mining scenes.
new.tip: Free; opening hours vary with the season.

new.title: Browse the Erzgebirgisches Spielzeugmuseum in Seiffen
new.desc: The Ore Mountain Toy Museum in Seiffen displays thousands of wooden toys, Christmas pyramids and nutcrackers made in the village over four centuries. It stands on Hauptstraße in the middle of the toy village.
new.tip: Open daily, around 10:00 to 17:00 per recent brochures; the open-air museum is further up the road.

new.title: Visit the octagonal Seiffen Bergkirche
new.desc: The Seiffener Bergkirche of 1779 is a baroque centralised church with a cupola and the symbol of the Ore Mountain toy village. Its shape inspired the Erzgebirge Christmas candle arches.
new.tip: Open weekdays around midday per recent brochures; confirm before a visit.

new.title: Tour Schloss Schwarzenberg above the Schwarzwasser
new.desc: Schloss Schwarzenberg is a Renaissance castle on a rock above the Ore Mountain town of Schwarzenberg and houses the town museum. The old town below also has a late Gothic town church.
new.tip: Allow two hours including the old town.

new.title: Reach the Fichtelberg, Saxony's highest summit
new.desc: The Fichtelberg at 1,215 m is the highest mountain in Saxony, with a weather station and the Fichtelberghaus summit hotel. On clear days the view reaches across the border to the Czech Klínovec peak.
new.tip: Check the weather; the cable car or the Fichtelbergbahn gets you close quickly.

new.title: Walk the Renaissance grid of Marienberg's Marktplatz
new.desc: Marienberg was laid out from 1521 as an ideal Renaissance town on a chessboard plan, one of the first planned mining towns in Saxony. Its huge Marktplatz has the Renaissance Rathaus and the Marienkirche.
new.tip: Free to wander.

new.title: Marvel at the Göltzsch Viaduct near Netzschkau
new.desc: The Göltzschtalbrücke is the world's largest brick bridge by volume, 78 m high and 574 m long, finished in 1851 for the Leipzig-Hof railway. About 26 million bricks were used and it is still in service.
new.tip: A viewing area on the Netzschkau side has good photo angles.

new.title: Discover Plauen lace in the Fabrik der Fäden
new.desc: The Plauen lace museum moved in 2023 into the Weisbachsches Haus, a former embroidery factory of 1776, as part of the German forum for textiles and lace. Plauen lace was a global industry from about 1900.
new.tip: Check opening days; the museum is on Bleichstraße.

new.title: Hear instruments at the Markneukirchen music museum
new.desc: The Musikinstrumenten-Museum is housed in the late baroque Paulusschlössel in Markneukirchen, centre of the Vogtland music corner. Instrument making here dates to the 17th century.
new.tip: Check opening days and demonstration times.

new.title: See the royal spa ensemble of Bad Elster
new.desc: Bad Elster was developed as a royal Saxon spa from 1848; the Königliches Kurhaus, the Albertbad and the park form the historic centre.
new.tip: Free to stroll the park; check the Chursächsische Philharmonie concert calendar.

new.title: Visit Altenburg's Residenzschloss and Playing Card Museum
new.desc: The castle on a porphyry rock above Altenburg was a ducal residence and has housed the Schloss- und Spielkartenmuseum. Altenburg is where Skat was devised around 1810, so the playing card museum is a stop for fans of the game.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday per recent flyers; a combined ticket exists with the Lindenau-Museum.

new.title: See Italian primitives at the Lindenau-Museum Altenburg
new.desc: The Lindenau-Museum was founded in 1848 by Bernhard von Lindenau and holds a large collection of Italian early Renaissance panel paintings. It also has a plaster cast collection and modern art.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; ticket about 4 euros.

new.title: Find the Skat Fountain in Altenburg
new.desc: The Skatbrunnen stands in Altenburg and honours the card game Skat, devised in the town around 1810. Its figures show playing card motifs.
new.tip: Free and always accessible.

new.title: Hike up the Pöhlberg above Annaberg
new.desc: The Pöhlberg is a 832 m basalt hill above Annaberg-Buchholz with a lookout tower and a mountain inn. It is the town's local mountain.
new.tip: Free; allow two hours round trip.

new.title: Climb the granite rocks of the Greifensteine
new.desc: The Greifensteine near Geyer are a cluster of granite rocks in the Ore Mountains that give a view across the Erzgebirge. A nature theatre and an old rock inn sit nearby.
new.tip: Entrance charge for the rocks; check summer performances.

new.title: Ride the steam Fichtelbergbahn from Cranzahl
new.desc: The Fichtelbergbahn is a 750 mm narrow-gauge steam railway running about 17 km from Cranzahl to Kurort Oberwiesenthal at the foot of the Fichtelberg. The 2026 timetable lists four pairs a day, with a break reported for November.
new.tip: Check dates before you travel; tickets are sold on board and at stations.

new.title: Ride the Fichtelberg cable car to the summit
new.desc: The Fichtelberg-Schwebebahn runs from Oberwiesenthal up the Fichtelberg. In winter it runs roughly 09:00 to 16:30.
new.tip: Pair it with a steam train arrival.

new.title: Go underground in the Reiche Zeche silver mine in Freiberg
new.desc: The Lehr- und Besucherbergwerk Reiche Zeche is part of the Freiberg mining university; guided tours go underground to show silver mining history. Tours run mid-week at fixed times, from about 18 euros.
new.tip: Bring a jacket; check tour times.

new.title: Tour the Zinngrube Ehrenfriedersdorf tin mine
new.desc: The Zinngrube Ehrenfriedersdorf is a visitor mine for tin ore worked since the 13th century. Guided tours go underground.
new.tip: Book via the mine; 2026 times not confirmed.

new.title: Visit the horse whim mine near Marienberg
new.desc: The Pferdegöpel Johannisstolln near Marienberg is a visitor mine with a horse whim that once hauled ore from the shaft.
new.tip: Check seasonal hours and tour dates.

new.title: Ride the Preßnitztalbahn from Jöhstadt
new.desc: The Preßnitztalbahn is a 750 mm narrow-gauge heritage railway in the Preßnitz valley between Jöhstadt and Steinbach with steam trains on operating days.
new.tip: Runs on set dates; check the calendar.

new.title: Watch a ring turner at the Seiffen open-air museum
new.desc: The Erzgebirgisches Freilichtmuseum in Seiffen shows a historic workshop for Reifendrehen, the craft of turning animal figures from rings of wood, unique to Seiffen.
new.tip: Open daily; the workshop pauses at midday.

new.title: Soak in the spa waters of Bad Elster
new.desc: Bad Elster has offered bathing since the 19th century; the historic Albertbad and the modern Soletherme use the town's mineral springs.
new.tip: Check hours and book spa treatments ahead.

new.title: Tour the Freiberger Brauhaus and taste Freiberger Pils
new.desc: The Freiberger Brauhaus offers a Brauhausführung following Freiberger Pils from raw material to finished product. Brewing in Freiberg goes back centuries.
new.tip: Book tours ahead by phone, 03731 3630.

new.title: Browse the Annaberg Christmas market around St. Anne
new.desc: The Annaberg Christmas market fills the Markt around the St. Annenkirche, with Erzgebirge pyramids, nutcrackers and Stollen. For 2026, listings give about 27 November to 23 December.
new.tip: Open later on Fridays and Saturdays; busy on Advent weekends.

new.title: Join the Freiberg Christmas market and Bergparade
new.desc: Freiberg's Christmas market on the Obermarkt is paired with a Bergparade of miners in uniform, listed for 6 December at 17:00 in torchlight.
new.tip: Dates shift yearly; check the city site.

new.title: Walk the Schwarzenberg Christmas market and Bergparade
new.desc: The Schwarzenberger Weihnachtsmarkt is held below the castle and features the Große Bergparade. For 2026 it is listed from 4 to 13 December with free entry.
new.tip: Visit in the evening for the lit castle.

new.title: Ski or sledge at the Fichtelberg resort
new.desc: Oberwiesenthal is a winter sports resort with ski runs on the Fichtelberg and a cable car to the summit, one of the main ski areas in eastern Germany.
new.tip: Snow varies; check conditions before travelling.

new.title: Order the Neunerlei at Ratskeller Zum Neinerlaa in Annaberg
new.desc: The Ratskeller Zum Neinerlaa on the Markt is named for the nine-course Ore Mountain Christmas meal. The dining rooms seat about 50 each and are decorated by season.
new.tip: Mains cost about 20 to 30 euros; check hours.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at Brauerei-Gasthof Zwönitz
new.desc: The Zwönitzer Brauerei revived local brewing in 1997 after 75 years without beer in town. The Gasthof on Grünhainer Straße serves hearty regional dishes, with a fireplace and a beer garden.
new.tip: Try the dark beer with a roast.

new.title: Taste Buttermilchgetzen at Oma's Kartoffelhaus
new.desc: Oma's Kartoffelhaus in Marienberg serves potato casseroles, baked potatoes, schnitzel variations and the Ore Mountain dish Buttermilchgetzen in a two-floor house with about 60 seats.
new.tip: Reserve on weekends.

new.title: Eat Saxon fare in the Freiberg Ratskeller
new.desc: The Ratskeller on the Obermarkt has been at this address since 1880 and serves hearty Saxon dishes under vaulted ceilings. The Schankhaus 1863 pub is in the same building.
new.tip: Book for the evening.

new.title: Have trout with red cabbage at the Pfeffersack in Freiberg
new.desc: The Historische Gastwirtschaft Pfeffersack serves Saxon dishes such as trout with red cabbage and potatoes in the old town of Freiberg.
new.tip: Check the current menu online.

new.title: Eat Vogtland cooking at Matsch, Plauen's oldest inn
new.desc: Matsch Gasthaus & Hotel on Nobelstraße is billed as Plauen's oldest tavern and is rated for regional Vogtland dishes. The evening kitchen opens from about 17:00.
new.tip: Try Vogtland Klöße with a roast.

new.title: Try herring with beetroot at Buntes Haus in Seiffen
new.desc: Restaurant Buntes Haus in Hotel Erbgericht on Hauptstraße serves Saxon dishes at about 9 to 23 euros, including herring Häckerle with beetroot. The chef updates Erzgebirge classics.
new.tip: Reserve in Advent.

new.title: Mix Erzgebirge and Bohemian dishes at Holzwurm in Seiffen
new.desc: Gaststätte Holzwurm blends Erzgebirge, Saxon and Bohemian cooking and has vegetarian options.
new.tip: Reservation requested; phone +49 37362 7277.

new.title: Eat home cooking at Gasthaus Gesecus in Altenburg
new.desc: Gasthaus Gesecus on the Topfmarkt is a very small Altenburg inn where the owner cooks regional dishes himself.
new.tip: Small, so book ahead.

new.title: Eat at the Erzgebirgsstuben in the Fichtelberghaus
new.desc: The Fichtelberghaus is the summit hotel at 1,215 m, and its Erzgebirgsstuben restaurant serves regional dishes.
new.tip: Reviews are mixed; check winter hours.

new.title: Order Buttermilchgetzen at the Ofenschenke in Hutha
new.desc: The Ofenschenke in Hutha near Olbernhau is a converted farmstead hotel and restaurant that serves the Erzgebirge dish Buttermilchgetzen.
new.tip: Book for weekends.

new.title: Book the Advent Neunerlei at the Dachsbaude in Neuhausen
new.desc: The Hotel Dachsbaude & Kammbaude in Neuhausen serves the nine-course Neunerlei on fixed dates, every Advent Sunday at 18:30 for groups of six or more.
new.tip: Advance booking is required.

new.title: Eat trout and Kaiserschmarrn at Hotel Vogtland in Bad Elster
new.desc: The restaurant in Hotel Vogtland in Bad Elster is recommended for trout from the Rauner Bach and Kaiserschmarrn.
new.tip: Reserve in the evening.

new.title: Sample local beer at Hotel Zum Alten Brauhaus in Oberwiesenthal
new.desc: The Hotel Zum Alten Brauhaus in Oberwiesenthal reports brewing since 1535 and has a restaurant.
new.tip: Check restaurant hours.
new.q: Hotel Zum Alten Brauhaus, Kurort Oberwiesenthal
